consensus_summary: Righteousness primarily denotes right standing before God (especially forensic/imputed righteousness credited by faith in Christ, not works) together with conformity to God's moral character/standard; often symbolized by a clean robe/garment; ethical living, infused transformation, covenant faithfulness, and social justice appear as related or alternative senses.
book_summary: Right-living: God Himself is the measure of right; for those under His authority it is the doing of His commandments (the law kept, worn as the garment of righteous acts). It is given and reckoned by grace (Rom 4 excludes only wage-work that would indebt God, not obedience itself), yet the gift never renames wrong-living right.
consensus_core_identification: Right standing before God (chiefly imputed by faith) plus conformity to God's standard (ethical quality/living).
book_core_identification: Right-living (doing God's commandments as duty, measured by His ways/works), reckoned by grace without ever renaming wrong-living as right.
boundary_disagreement: Book treats actual obedience/right-living as definitional and excludes any reckoning that would cover or rename wrong-living; consensus admits forensic status for imperfect believers, treating right-living chiefly as fruit/evidence rather than the core itself.
rationale: Both readings share the general category of rightness according to God, received by grace through faith rather than meritorious wages. The book preserves that category while narrowing its extension and altering priority/conditions: it elevates the ethical/behavioral sense (commandment-keeping as garment of acts, duty not wage) to the definitional core, explicitly rejects the common status-first framing (right-living merely subsequent fruit), and bars the gift from applying to wrong-living. This is boundary refinement, not replacement of the central referent.
strongest_objection: The book's refusal to let reckoned righteousness cover wrong-living undercuts the classic forensic reading of Romans 4 and the simul justus et peccator framework, potentially collapsing justification into sanctification and sidelining the garment-as-covering imagery dominant in the consensus.
